source_row.stem: Under a value-based purchasing program, hospital reimbursement is influenced by several factors, and a finance colleague assumes reimbursement really just comes down to how many services the hospital happens to bill for. Under this program, reimbursement is instead influenced by:
source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Primarily the volume of services a hospital provides, without any measured quality component involved, similar to what the finance colleague is currently assuming","B":"A largely random process without any defined, measurable criteria behind the reimbursement decision, contrary to the structured criteria this program actually uses","C":"Measured quality performance and patient outcomes, not just volume of services, rather than volume alone as the finance colleague is currently assuming","D":"Mainly the physical size of the facility, rather than any measure of the care actually delivered, which does not describe how this program actually works"}}
source_row.rationale: Value-based purchasing programs tie a portion of hospital reimbursement to measured quality performance and patient outcomes, rather than solely the volume of services provided.
